_comment: Hand-maintained. The Python and C++ surfaces are small and change rarely, so they are not machine-derived the way the R index is (scripts/sync-content.R). Keep in step with pyexuber/src/exuber/__init__.py and exubercore/include/exubercore/radf.hpp.

python.note: Bindings over exubercore. Monte Carlo and wild-bootstrap critical values are ported; the sieve bootstrap (radf_sb_cv), the second wild-bootstrap variant (radf_wb_cv2), and the summary/tidy/diagnostics layer are not yet.

cpp.note: The statistic itself, and nothing else — Armadillo only, no R or Python dependency. Both bindings call this one function. The lag == 0 closed form is bit-reproducible across toolchains; the lag > 0 Sherman-Morrison path agrees to ~1e-12 but is not bit-identical.

entries.name: arma::vec radf(const arma::mat& yxmat, int min_win, int lag = 0)
entries.title: Returns badf[0, total), adf, sadf, gsadf, then bsadf[total+3, 2*total+3), where total = nrow(yxmat) - min_win + 1
